new_statements.quote: TONEN. De tonen zijn als in lonkundo. Ook de tonetische regels verschillen niet. Zoo bv. het bewaren der tonen in elisie: en de uitzondering daarop bij prefixen e en o: bv. nsé ené wordt ns'éné = deze visch; botômôlô onâmi: botômôl'ônâmi = mijn oudere broeder.
new_statements.translation: TONES. The tones are as in Lonkundo. The tonetic rules do not differ either. Thus e.g. the preservation of the tones under elision, and the exception to it with the prefixes e and o: e.g. nsé ené becomes ns'éné 'this fish'; botômôlô onâmi: botômôl'ônâmi 'my elder brother'.

new_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened, extracted PDF pages 96-101 with extracted text and rendered PDF page 99 (printed p. 97) to an image and read it. The TONEN paragraph is there as quoted: "TONEN. De tonen zijn als in lonkundo. Ook de tonetische regels verschillen niet. Zoo bv. het bewaren der tonen in elisie; en de uitzondering daarop bij prefixen e en o: bv. nsé ené wordt ns'éné = deze visch; botómóló onámi: botómól'ónámi = mijn oude-re b oeder." Minor differences only: the print has the typo "b oeder" for "broeder" (the report silently corrects it) and the report normalises the tone diacritics to circumflexes. The article "Over het dialekt der Boyela" runs printed pp. 95-98 (PDF 97-100): intro on the Boyela of the…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The language (Boyela/Loyela dialect of the Tshuapa) is described as a tone language whose tones and tone rules are those of Lonkundo (Mongo); the source gives no rule for word stress or accent placement.
new_statements.exceptions: Only tonal: tones are kept under elision except with the prefixes e and o. In the 1942 continuation (p. 15) one item, the indefinite numeral -nkumélâ 'all', is annotated 'prefix hoog, klemtoon op e' (high prefix, stress/prominence on e) — a lexical note, not a general rule.
new_statements.domain_note: Word and phrase level tone in citation and elided forms; no domain statement for stress because none is described.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted source describes the Boyela (Loyela) dialect of the Tshuapa (notes taken at Bondombe and Ikela schools from Bankanja-Mbalá, Likolómwá, Bokétsi, Sónjo and Endé speakers), i.e. the Yela (C74) side of Glottolog's yela1238 'Yela-Kela'; Hulstaert notes outsiders call them Bakela/Akela. Forges 1977 and Ikosso 1994 describe the Kela/Ikela (C75, Lomela) side, which Glottolog merges into the same languoid; Hulstaert 1982 says the Lomela Ekûkû differ little from the Tshuapa Boyela. Hulstaert treats Loyela as a Mongo (lonkundo) dialect, so his tone statement is by reference to Lonkundo.

new_statements.translation: TONES. The tones are as in Lonkundo. The tonetic rules do not differ either. Thus e.g. the preservation of the tones in elision; and the exception to that with the prefixes e and o: e.g. nsé ené becomes ns'éné = this fish; botómóló onámi : botómól'ónámi = my elder brother. [1942, p. 15:] Indefinite numerals: -umélá or -nkumélá (prefix high, accent on e) = all

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: lines 4619-4627 (printed p. 97 = PDF page 99) and the page scan show: 'TONEN. De tonen zijn als in lonkundo. Ook de tonetische regels verschillen niet. Zoo bv. het bewaren der tonen in elisie; en de uitzondering daarop bij prefixen e en o : bv. nsé ené wordt ns'éné = deze visch; botómóló onámi : botómól'ónámi = mijn oude-re b oeder.' the compiler quote matches the print except that it silently normalises the print typo 'oude-re b oeder' to 'oudere broeder'; the acute accents (botómóló onámi) are as in the image, whereas the catalog's existing statement carries scanned circumflexes (botômôlô onâmi), which should be corrected to acutes. The 1942 half of the quote is verified in line 632-633 a…
new_statements.relation_note: Identical to the existing statement (same TONEN paragraph, verified against the page scan; diacritics in print are acute accents: botómóló onámi : botómól'ónámi). Confirms the catalog's 'tone language, no stress statement' reading. The line 'het intensiteitsaccent valt op de voorlaatste lettergreep van het woord' on Aequatoria 5 (1942) p. 44 is NOT part of this article: it is in the Epistolaria piece 'Talen rond het Kivu-meer' (about Kivu languages such as ekiyira/mashi), printed after Hulstaert's signature at the end of the Boyela article on p. 43.
new_statements.rule_in_words: The sketch treats Boyela as a tone language whose tones and tone rules are those of Lonkundo (Mongo-Nkundo); it gives no rule for word stress anywhere in the 1941 article or the 1942 continuation. The single word 'klemtoon' occurs only as a lexical note on the numeral -nkumélá ('accent on e', alongside 'prefix high'), i.e. a tone-marking note on one item, not a stress rule.
new_statements.exceptions: Tonal only: tones are preserved under elision except after the prefixes e and o (1941 p. 97); the verb yâ 'come' sometimes takes low tone, with the person prefix also going low (1942 p. 41).
new_statements.identity_note: Hulstaert 1941/42 describes the Boyela (loyela) dialect of the Tshuapa (notes taken at the schools of Bondombe and Ikela from Bankanja-Mbalá, Likolómwá, Bokétsi, Sónjo and Endé speakers), which he places close to the north-west Mongo dialect (Lonkundo); he says the Ekûkû of the Lomela differ little, while the Bambuli of the Lomami use 'a wholly different dialect'. Forges 1977 (not opened) describes Kela of the Lomela confines (Guthrie C75), the other half of the Glottolog languoid yela1238 Yela-Kela.
